styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small clothes rack with shirts on a grey stand. This is not a clear match for the reference quality, so it fails.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small clothing rack with shirts on a grey disc base. The measured facts are mixed. Visible tones per tile (15) are close to the stall (17) and well (20), and near-flat coverage is 0%, so it is not a flat-fill piece. But 76% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 0-1% on the tinted hedge and stall references and 33% on the well. Together with the dark grey/black rim and hanger line visible in the image, this reads as a neutral near-black outline rather than a dark tone of the adjacent material. Each shirt shows only about 2-3 steps (a base colour, a shade and a dark edge), and the base disc is similarly shallow. That is below the 5-6 steps per material on the references. The piece has only 21 distinct colours in total, against 38-40 on the rich references. The small size and the grouping of shirts into blocks of colour leave little grain or per-item highlighting. The 15 tones per tile come mostly from many different materials packed into one tile, not from deep shading of any one material. A careful artist would find it sticker-like next to the stall and well.
